knowledge_point.title: Calculating Flux Across a Closed Surface

question.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=0$, $x=3$, $y=0$, $y=4$, $z=0$, $z=2$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(2x+1)\,i+3z\,j+xy\,k$, find the flux of $F$ across $S$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x+1)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy) \\  & =2+0+0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}2\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}2\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}z \\  & =[2x]_{x=0}^{x=3}\cdot (4-0)\cdot (2-0) \\  & =(6-0)\cdot 4\cdot 2 \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=3,$ $y=-1,$ $y=2,$ $z=\frac{\pi}{2},$ $z=\frac{3 \pi}{2}.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,j+(x+y)\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+y) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z+0+0 \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}2x\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{2}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{\pi /2}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=3}\cdot (2-(-1))\cdot [\operatorname{sin}⁡z]_{z=\pi /2}^{z=\frac{3 \pi}{2}} \\  & =({3}^{2}-{1}^{2})\cdot 3\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3 \pi}{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi}{2})) \\  & =8\cdot 3\cdot -2 \\  & =-48.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x =0$, $x = 3$, $y = 0$, $y = 1$, $z = 1$, $z = 4$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F = 2xzi + (x^{2} + z)j + 2k$, find the flux of $F$ across $S$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xz)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x^{2} + z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2) \\  & =2z+0+0 \\  & =2z.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2z\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{4}2z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{1}^{4}2z\,\text{d}z \\  & =(3-0)\cdot (1-0)\cdot [{z}^{2}]_{z=1}^{z=4} \\  & =3\cdot 1\cdot (16-1) \\  & =45.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1$, $x=3$, $y=1$, $y=3$, $z=0$, $z=2$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F={e}^{z}\,i+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,j+4{x}^{2}yz\,k$, find the flux of $F$ across $S$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{z})+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(4{x}^{2}yz) \\  & =0+2 x^{2} y+4 x^{2} y \\  & =6{x}^{2}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{1}^{3}2y\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{3}]_{x=1}^{x=3}\cdot [{y}^{2}]_{y=1}^{y=3}\cdot (2-0) \\  & =(27-1)\cdot (9-1)\cdot 2 \\  & =416.\end{aligned}
$$
